name: Levonorgestrel
route_note: single oral tablet for emergency contraception; intrauterine system lasting up to 8 years; subdermal implant
originator: Wyeth (norgestrel synthesised by Herchel Smith); Schering AG developed many levonorgestrel products

discovery.note: Total synthesis of racemic norgestrel; the active levorotatory enantiomer, levonorgestrel, was later developed on its own.

rx_status: OTC for emergency contraception in many countries; prescription for IUD and implant
tagline: Widely used progestin for emergency contraception, IUDs and implants
summary: Levonorgestrel is a synthetic progestin used alone for emergency contraception, in hormonal intrauterine systems and implants, and with an oestrogen in combined pills. A single oral dose taken soon after unprotected sex mainly works by delaying ovulation. The levonorgestrel IUD is also used for heavy menstrual bleeding.
mechanism: Levonorgestrel binds and activates progesterone receptors. Continuous exposure thickens cervical mucus, which blocks sperm penetration, and suppresses the mid-cycle surge of luteinising hormone.

As emergency contraception, a high single dose before the LH surge postpones or prevents ovulation; it is not effective once ovulation has occurred and does not disrupt an implanted pregnancy. Locally released levonorgestrel in the intrauterine system thins the endometrium, reducing menstrual bleeding.
uses: Long-acting contraception (intrauterine system and subdermal implant)
Endometrial protection during oestrogen therapy (some intrauterine systems)

history.title: Norgestrel synthesised
history.detail: Herchel Smith's group achieves total synthesis of norgestrel.

history.title: Norplant
history.detail: The FDA approves the levonorgestrel Norplant implant; the levonorgestrel IUD is introduced in Finland.

history.title: WHO trial
history.detail: Levonorgestrel alone proves more effective and better tolerated than the oestrogen–progestin Yuzpe regimen for emergency contraception.

history.title: Plan B
history.detail: FDA approves Plan B two-tablet emergency contraception.

history.title: Mirena in US
history.detail: FDA approves the Mirena levonorgestrel intrauterine system.

history.title: OTC access
history.detail: Plan B becomes available without prescription in the US for adults.

history.title: No age limit
history.detail: After court rulings, Plan B One-Step becomes available OTC without age restriction in the US.

facts: Enzyme-inducing drugs such as rifampicin and carbamazepine reduce levonorgestrel levels, and a double dose or copper IUD is advised for emergency contraception.
Efficacy of oral emergency contraception declines the longer it is delayed after intercourse, within the labelled 72 hours.
